lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Lakeside Golf Club | Caddie | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Caddied about 5 rounds a week, carrying bags and reading greens for members.
- Helped the pro shop run the weekend junior tournament.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved close efficiency by 40% by automating reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Wrote the variance commentary for the monthly board pack, explaining each line more than 5% off budget.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Reported a 45% group EBITDA margin by adding the EBITDA margins of the three business units.
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Underwrote 60 small-business loans worth USD 45M, and none of the approved loans defaulted in their first two years.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Tested the valuation's sensitivity: a 1-point change in the discount rate moved the share value from USD 52 to USD 44.
- Shared the model and a two-page note with the university investment club, which used it in its spring pitch.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Built an 18-month cash forecast for a USD 600M business, holding error to about 4% and freeing USD 40M to repay debt early.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Bloomberg Terminal
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: The current caddie role leads Experience instead of the two finance roles.
items.because: Placing it first makes non-finance work define the page before the reader reaches the finance roles.

items.says: The move from finance employment to the current caddie role is unexplained.
items.because: A finance reader may wonder whether it reflects a career shift or an interim role.

items.says: Education appears before several years of finance experience.
items.because: Leading with Education delays the stronger examples in the analyst roles.

items.says: The caddie duties do not show a benefit beyond completing them.
“Caddied” uses past tense for a role listed as current.
The tournament line does not identify the task handled.
items.because: “Helped” gives the reader no way to tell which event responsibility was yours.

items.says: The tournament is named without a result of your contribution.
“Helped” uses past tense for a role listed as current.
The 40% close-efficiency improvement does not identify its measure or comparison.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what improved or assess the gain without a baseline.

items.says: The explanation of standardized project rules is wordy.
The board-pack commentary does not say what it enabled.
The variance threshold does not show the analysis behind the explanations.
“Each line” can be mistaken for a line of commentary rather than a financial line item.
Discounting free cash flow to equity at WACC uses the wrong discount rate.
items.because: Free cash flow to equity is discounted at the cost of equity; WACC pairs with free cash flow to the firm.

items.says: The acquisition valuation does not say how it was used.
Adding business-unit EBITDA margins does not calculate a group EBITDA margin.
items.because: Margins are ratios, not amounts that can be summed, so the stated method makes the 45% figure unreliable.

items.says: The group-margin output does not say what the reporting informed.
The same forecast achievement is attributed to Stonebridge and the Student Investment Fund.
items.because: The matching figures appear under dates years apart, putting both entries’ credibility at risk.

items.says: The strongest Stonebridge result is buried after the opening bullet.
items.because: It connects measurable forecast accuracy to USD 40M of early debt repayment.

items.says: The debt-repayment outcome sits too far behind the forecast description.
The loan count does not show the analysis behind the underwriting.
The no-defaults clause is wordy.
The declined-application review does not say what it found or compared.
items.because: The missing reasoning would show credit judgment rather than only the outcome.

items.says: The approval-rate result is not the opening Crescent Bank bullet.
items.because: Its specific impact would establish the role before the broader underwriting-volume claim.

items.says: “My findings” introduces first person into the résumé bullet.
“Writes” presents work in a role that ended in December 2022 as ongoing.
items.because: Present tense implies a current responsibility that conflicts with the end date.

items.says: The checklist line does not identify the control that reduced missed tests.
The credit-memo wording makes the memo, rather than preparation time, sound like what was cut.
The utility and the date anchoring the market-price comparison are unidentified.
items.because: A reader cannot readily assess what was valued or verify which observed price the 6% result uses.

items.says: The discount-rate change has no direction.
The club’s use of the valuation is unspecified.
The FP&A line does not identify your action, deliverable or its effect and pulls the entry away from fund work.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what you produced or achieved, and the broad claim weakens the entry beside the specific fund report.

items.says: “Financial reporting and analysis” is too broad to show the finance skill used.
items.because: Those categories cover many tasks and do not identify the report or analysis produced.

items.says: The fund performance report is not the entry’s opening bullet.
items.because: Its benchmark comparison and recurring committee use give a clearer account of the role than the broad FP&A opening.

items.says: The committee-use clause can be shorter.
The 4% forecast-error claim does not say what was compared.
items.because: Without that comparison, a reader cannot assess how the accuracy figure was determined.

items.says: The cash-forecast line does not show the forecasting approach.
items.because: A reader sees the horizon and claimed result but not the analytical work that produced the forecast.
